evidence.publisher: Journal Officiel de la République Démocratique du Congo
evidence.source_title: Journal Officiel, Première partie, numéro 2, 15 janvier 2012
evidence.observation: The official DRC record identifies the 8 July 2011 crash of Hewa Bora Airways Boeing 727-100 and states that it caused loss of human life; it records the Transport Ministry action taken after the accident.

NTSB identifies Hewa Bora Boeing 727-100 9Q-COP as domestic scheduled commercial flight 952, reports 77 fatalities, and explicitly states that the Government of the DRC was conducting the investigation.

provenance_caveat: A canonical-host DRC final investigation report was not located. The competent-state requirement is satisfied here by an official DRC government publication establishing the crash and loss of life, reconciled with the NTSB accredited-representative record that identifies the DRC government as investigator. This caveat remains public and no secondary cause narrative is promoted as authority fact.

completeness_assessment.reason: The fatal Western-built jet universe and Boeing membership are mapped; First Air, Asiana and Iran Air have competent-authority documentation, while Hewa Bora is supported by an official DRC government publication plus NTSB accredited-representative evidence identifying the DRC investigation. Independent annual reconciliation is present and no unresolved target-taxonomy issue changes 2011 membership.
